title: FastAPI: dependency injection, lifespan and settings
description: FastAPI dependencies and their per-request caching, overrides in tests, lifespan startup and shutdown per worker, and typed configuration with pydantic-settings.
source: FastAPI documentation (dependencies with yield, lifespan events, testing dependency overrides); pydantic-settings documentation; Python functools documentation (lru_cache); Uvicorn deployment documentation
seriesDescription: FastAPI structure and Depends, routing and Pydantic validation, error handling, middleware, async, API design, jobs and health. JEE-Advanced style: integer, assertion-reason, matrix match, fill-in-the-blanks, short code and multi-correct questions.

questions.prompt: In FastAPI, write a GET route /users/{user_id} named read_user that receives a db session from a dependency get_db via Depends and declares response_model=UserOut. Return db.get_user(user_id).
questions.explanation: Depends(callable) makes FastAPI call get_db per request and pass the result in. async def and Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)] are equally valid forms.

questions.prompt: How do you replace the real get_db dependency with a fake in a FastAPI test?

options.why: The override dict is keyed by the original callable and is the documented way.

options.text: Use unittest.mock.patch on the Depends class itself, then call the client.
options.why: Depends is evaluated at import time in the signature; patching it later does nothing.

options.text: Restart the app with an environment variable named GET_DB.
options.why: FastAPI has no such lookup; dependencies are resolved from callables.

options.text: Pass the fake through TestClient(app, db=fake).
options.why: TestClient does not accept dependency arguments.

questions.explanation: Remember to clear app.dependency_overrides after the test (a fixture with yield). The key must be the exact function object used in Depends().

questions.prompt: A route has two sub-dependencies a() and b(); both declare Depends(get_conn). The route itself also declares conn = Depends(get_conn, use_cache=False). With default settings, how many times does get_conn run for one request?
questions.explanation: Within one request FastAPI caches a dependency result, so a() and b() share one get_conn call. use_cache=False forces a separate call, giving 2.

questions.prompt: APP_DB_URL is set both as an OS environment variable and in the .env file read by a pydantic-settings BaseSettings (env_prefix='APP_'). Nothing is passed to the constructor. Which value does db_url get?

options.text: The OS environment variable; it outranks .env.
options.why: Environment variables outrank the dotenv file in pydantic-settings.

options.text: The .env file value, because it is more specific.
options.why: Dotenv sits below real environment variables in the priority order.

options.text: Whichever was loaded last, so it is non-deterministic.
options.why: The order is fixed: init kwargs, env vars, dotenv, secrets dir, defaults.

options.text: The class default, because both sources are ignored.
options.why: Defaults are only used when no source supplies the field.

questions.explanation: Priority (highest first): init arguments, environment variables, .env, secrets directory, field defaults. Verified by running it.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: FastAPI lifespan startup code runs once per worker process before it accepts requests.
questions.reason: A uvicorn deployment with four workers executes the lifespan startup only once for all workers.

whys.b: Wrong: R is not true, so this cannot be b.
whys.c: Correct: each worker is a separate process with its own app and lifespan run, so 4 workers means 4 startups (4 pools, 4 caches).

questions.explanation: Per-process startup matters for connection pools (size them as workers x pool size) and for one-off work such as migrations, which belongs in a deploy step, not lifespan.

questions.prompt: Write a FastAPI lifespan handler: an async context manager lifespan(app) that creates app.state.pool = await create_pool() on startup and awaits app.state.pool.close() on shutdown, then pass it to FastAPI.
questions.starter:
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI
questions.model:
@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app):
    app.state.pool = await create_pool()
    yield
    await app.state.pool.close()

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
questions.explanation: Lifespan replaces the deprecated on_event startup/shutdown hooks. Use try/finally around yield if shutdown must run even on error.

questions.prompt: Write a FastAPI dependency get_db that creates a session with SessionLocal(), yields it to the route, and always closes it afterwards, even if the route raises.
questions.explanation: Code after yield is the teardown; the try/finally makes it run even when the route fails. A with SessionLocal() as db: yield db block is an equivalent spelling.

questions.prompt: Write a pydantic-settings class Settings that reads variables with the prefix APP_ (env_prefix) from the environment and from a .env file, with database_url: str (required) and debug: bool = False.
questions.model:
class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="APP_", env_file=".env")

    database_url: str
    debug: bool = False
questions.explanation: APP_DATABASE_URL then binds to database_url (verified by running it). A missing required value raises a ValidationError at startup, which is the fail-fast behaviour you want. Wrap Settings() in an lru_cache function so it is built once.

questions.text: A {1} subclass binds environment variables to typed fields; typing a value as {2} hides it in repr and logs; the real value is read with {3}().
questions.explanation: SecretStr prints as ********. model_dump() would still expose the value in some cases, so ship secrets through get_secret_value() only at the point of use.

questions.prompt: Match each FastAPI construct with its job.

right.text: Builds a per-request collaborator and injects it into the handler
Runs startup code before serving and shutdown code afterwards, once per worker process
Swaps a dependency for a fake, typically in tests
Holds application-wide objects such as a connection pool
Runs a function after the response has been sent

questions.explanation: The first three answer "how do I wire things": dependencies for per-request objects, lifespan for process-wide resources, overrides for testing. BackgroundTasks and exception handlers are separate features.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: Decorating a get_settings() function with functools.lru_cache means the Settings object is built once per process.
questions.reason: lru_cache returns the stored result when a function is called again with the same arguments.

whys.a: Correct: get_settings() takes no arguments, so every call after the first returns the cached object.

questions.explanation: Combine with Depends(get_settings) so tests can override it, and call get_settings.cache_clear() when a test changes environment variables.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)] and db: Session = Depends(get_db) resolve the dependency identically at runtime.
questions.reason: Annotated lets a dependency declaration be stored in a reusable type alias.

whys.a: Wrong: reusability is a convenience and does not explain identical runtime behaviour.
whys.b: Correct: both are true, but R is a benefit of Annotated, not the reason the two forms behave the same.

questions.explanation: Annotated also keeps default values free for real defaults and works better with type checkers. Define DbDep = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)] once and reuse it.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: FastAPI calls a dependency function once, when the module is imported, and reuses its result for every request.
questions.reason: Dependencies are declared in the signature of the route, which is evaluated at import time.

whys.d: Correct: the declaration Depends(get_db) is created at import time, but the dependency function is called anew for each request (and cached only within one request).

questions.explanation: For an object that must live for the whole process, create it in lifespan and store it on app.state, or wrap the factory in lru_cache.

questions.prompt: A lifespan startup handler loads a 200 MB lookup table into memory. The service runs with 4 uvicorn worker processes on one machine. Roughly how many MB of memory do the tables occupy in total?
questions.explanation: Each worker is a separate process with its own application and lifespan run, so every worker holds its own copy: 4 x 200 = 800 MB. Shared read-only data needs shared memory, a memory-mapped file or an external cache such as Redis.

questions.prompt: Write the test setup lines that replace get_db with fake_get_db for a FastAPI app, create a TestClient named client, and clear all overrides again after the test.
questions.model:
app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = fake_get_db
client = TestClient(app)
# ... run the test ...
app.dependency_overrides.clear()
questions.explanation: Put the clear() call in a pytest fixture after yield so it runs even when the test fails. The override key must be the exact function object used in Depends().
